thread:
marta: Heads-up — kicking off BluePlum private deploy prep. Main blockers I want to get ironed out asap: registry sync approach, cert validation egress, and who owns CA import for the airgapped boxes.

leo: Re netops side — we have a JIT egress tunnel pattern we can stand up for validation, but it needs infra approval + a CIDR allowlist from you.

sam: I started the approval ticket INC-4821 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4821). Waiting on security ACK (Mark) for outbound proxy rules. ETA end of day.

anya: For smoke we should prefer an offline image bundle to avoid registry churn. If BluePlum insists on sync, we need a single host allowed to reach registry.redwood.internal (52.23.11.5:443) and the CA fingerprint.

marta: Good call. BluePlum ops asked for registry sync to make image rollouts easier for them. I'll send the minimal host list in a sec. Also plan: canary = 1 node, health checks + model fallback to v1.9 if image pull fails.

carl-netops: @marta send the host IPs + desired source CIDRs. We can configure a temporary NAT + proxy tunnel to our egress jumpbox. We need the cert thumbprint (sha256).

marta: thumbprint: 3f:8a:bd:11:cc:9d:7e:2f:5a:01:44:bf:9e:6b:4a:12:77:de:aa:90:12:34:56:78:9a:bc:de:ef:01:23:45

leo: Copy that. netops will also need the list of ports. Registry only needs 443 outbound. If they require ACME/OCSP checks, we may need 80/443 to ocsp.intel-ca.example too. Confirm whether OCSP stapling is used on Redwood registry.

anya: We run OCSP stapling on the registry, but BluePlum's internal proxy might attempt OCSP directly. Recommend allowing 443 to ocsp.acme-ca.example (34.201.22.7).

sam: From infra: temporary egress policy looks fine. Two asks: (1) who approves the JIT window (we prefer timeboxed), (2) can SRE own post-canary rollbacks?

marta: (1) Approver = @sam + @leo. I'll schedule a 2-hour window tomorrow 09:00-11:00 UTC. (2) SRE (anya) to own rollback/runbook.

leo: I'll queue the firewall change for that window, subject to Mark's security signoff on the ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job queued: blueplum-private-canary-20241216. Status: pending. Trigger window: 2024-12-16T09:15Z -> 09:45Z.

anya: Quick runbook notes: smoke checks = (1) image pull succeeded, (2) process up, (3) healthcheck /v1/health OK, (4) sample inference run under 500ms p50. If any fail -> immediate rollback to model v1.9 and notify #oncall.

marta: Ownership matrix so it's clear: rollout lead = marta, egress owner = carl-netops, infra approvals/ticket = sam, rollback + smoke = anya. I'll paste this into the ticket.

carl-netops: One more network question — do we need DNS rewrite to point registry.redwood.internal to the proxy IP inside BluePlum? That'd avoid cross-host routing issues.

marta: Yes, BluePlum prefers internal DNS remap. We'll coordinate with their infra to update /etc/hosts or their internal DNS zone.

sam: I'll add DNS change and rollback steps to INC-4821. Also adding a line: revoke JIT after window.

marta: Thanks all. Next steps for today: 1) I send host list + CIDRs, 2) sam pushes approval and DNS stub, 3) carl wires JIT egress, 4) anya finalizes runbook. If nothing blocks we'll run canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

leo: Ping me here when Mark signs off, I’ll kick firewall rule.

anya: I’ll prep the smoke script and put it in the ticket as a gist.

marta: Gist: https://gist.github.com/marta/blueplum-canary-smoke (contains the curl/checks + rollback cli).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: canary job will auto-abort if preflight healthchecks fail within first 10 minutes.

marta: Cool — closing the loop here. If any new blockers pop up drop a quick note.
